historical_growth.growth_rate_source: TTM organic run-rate (pro forma revenue growth 2.0-3.0% through 2026)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-7.5%, FY2022-FY2025) diverges from revenue CAGR (+7.1%) by more than 30%: equity is shrinking through buybacks and accumulated losses, so it is not a usable growth anchor. The selected rate is the current organic run-rate instead.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGR is the company's own continuing-operations figure for 2022-2025 (FY2025 10-K). No 5-year figures: periods before FY2023 include the divested marketing technology business and are not comparable. EPS moved from loss to profit, so no CAGR. Owner FCF (OCF less PP&E less capitalised software less SBC less RSU withholding taxes): FY2023 56.5, FY2024 64.7, FY2025 45.0, TTM 35.1 -- falling while reported FCF was roughly flat (81.5, 94.3, 79.6), because capitalised software rose from 17.4 to 32.4 and RSU withholding taxes from 0 to 8.4. Revenue growth has also decelerated sharply inside the window: 4.8% in FY2025, ~3% in 2026.

scenario_narratives.base: Organic growth stays near today's 3% and drifts to ~4% as integrated payments attach and the ZyraTalk AI engagement product cross-sell into the home-services (EverPro) and health (EverHealth) bases, but net revenue retention, which slid from 97% to 93% through 2026, only stabilises rather than recovering. The transformation programme winds down, so the 'non-recurring' costs that have run at ~3% of revenue for four years roughly halve and the cash EBITDA margin moves from 25% to 27.5%. SBC plus withholding taxes eases from 6.3% to 5% of revenue, capitalised software stays near 5.5%, and cash tax normalises to 25% as shields run off. The term loan is serviced comfortably and refinanced before July 2031.
scenario_narratives.bull: Payments penetration of the existing 700k+ customer base and AI-agent upsell re-accelerate growth to 6-7%, retention returns to the high 90s, and the simplified two-vertical structure delivers real operating leverage: cash EBITDA margin reaches 31% (company adjusted EBITDA in the low-to-mid 30s) with transformation costs gone. SBC falls to 4.5% of revenue. This needs both the growth re-acceleration and the cost exit to happen; neither is visible in the 2026 numbers.
scenario_narratives.bear: Retention keeps falling: SMB customers in home services and small medical practices churn to AI-native or horizontal tools (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro, payment-led suites), and a soft SMB economy trims payment volumes. Revenue stalls for three years and recovers only to ~2%. Defending the base keeps product spend and 'transformation' costs elevated, so the cash margin slips to 23.5-24% and SBC stays at 6%+. With ~$384M of net debt, the equity takes the whole hit: enterprise value falls by about a third and equity value by more than half.

valuation_philosophy.summary: EverCommerce screens cheaply on company-adjusted EBITDA (~8x EV) but most of that EBITDA does not reach owners: of ~174 of TTM adjusted EBITDA, ~26 is capitalised commissions and recurring 'non-recurring' costs, ~38 is SBC plus RSU withholding taxes, ~34 is capex (mostly capitalised software) and ~31 is cash interest. Levered owner FCF is ~35 on a ~$1.06B market cap. The valuation therefore rests on a cash margin, not adjusted EBITDA, and the leverage makes the per-share value highly sensitive to margin and growth assumptions.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net revenue retention (93% in Q3-2026, from 97% a year earlier): a further decline pushes the business toward the bear path.
The treatment of 'transaction-related and other non-recurring' costs: if they genuinely stop, the base case is ~1-1.5 margin points too low; if they continue at 3% of revenue, it is too high.
Leverage: $522.5M term loan due July 2031 against ~$1.06B of equity; each 1pp of terminal cash margin is worth roughly $0.40-0.50 a share.
Cash tax ramp is a judgment: the NOL balance and Section 382 limits were not read from the tax note.
Sponsor control (~85.7%) and a thin float: a take-private or block sale would set the price outside this framework.
SBC: Q3-2026 expense jumped to 11.5 from ~5.8 in each of the prior two quarters; if that is a new run-rate rather than a one-off acceleration, the 6.3% starting charge is too low.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.01-14.41 (the price is at the 52-week low).
data_sources.financials: SEC filings in research/EVCM/Extracted: 10-K FY2025 (continuing-operations income statement, adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, cash flow, debt note) and 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet at 2026-09-30, nine-month cash flow, share count, term loan); EVCM.duckdb core_metrics and kpis.
data_sources.qualitative: 10-K FY2025 business and risk sections and 10-Q Q3-2026 MD&A; no Analysis JSON existed at build time.

inputs.share_count_basis: 175.675M shares issued and outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) plus ~1.04M treasury-method dilution (Q3 diluted less basic weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. A further 14.7M options/RSUs were anti-dilutive in Q3 and are not in the count; their cost is carried by the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30, continuing operations: SBC expense 29.55 (FY2025 10-K adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation 27.929, less 9M-2025 21.551, plus 9M-2026 23.172) plus employee taxes paid for RSU withholdings 8.39 (financing activities: 6.722 - 5.250 + 6.915). The filer publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.3 for a sponsor-controlled, thinly floated small cap -> cost of equity ~10.8%. Term loan at SOFR + 2.25% (6.15% at 2026-09-30), ~4.6% after tax, at ~27% of enterprise value -> blended ~9.1%; rounded up to 9.5% for the float and size. One WACC for all three scenarios: scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and the weights, not by the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for a software company; lease cost sits inside EBITDA and lease liabilities are not added to net debt.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company: tech, SaaS'). Fresh build, no prior valuation. BASE IS CONTINUING OPERATIONS ONLY: the marketing technology business was divested in October 2025 and is in discontinued operations; base revenue is TTM to 2026-09-30 on the restated continuing basis (FY2025 588.907 - 9M-2025 437.754 + 9M-2026 450.927 = 602.08). Year 1 is therefore the twelve months to September 2027, matching the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. EBITDA MARGIN IS A CASH MARGIN, NOT COMPANY ADJUSTED EBITDA: TTM adjusted EBITDA is 174.4 (29.0%), but that adds back amortisation of capitalised contract-acquisition costs (~7.1 TTM, a cash commission cost) and 'transaction-related and other non-recurring' costs that have recurred every year (17.5 / 26.4 / 19.8 in FY2023-25, ~18.9 TTM). Stripping both gives ~24.7%, which reconciles to cash: TTM OCF 107.3 + cash interest ~31.5 + cash tax 2.8 = ~141.6 (23.5%) before a ~8 working-capital drag. reported_fcf = TTM OCF 107.31 less PP&E 1.92 less capitalised software 32.39 (the Metrics CSV capex column carries PP&E only; capitalised software is the larger line and is included in capex here). FY2025 and 9M-2025 OCF are consolidated and include the divested business, so TTM OCF has a small discontinued-operations residual. last_fcf is LEVERED (after ~31.5 of cash interest) and is retained for audit only; the projections are unlevered and net debt is deducted in the bridge. Interest income not stripped: the company is in net debt. Net debt uses the term-loan face value (522.5), not the carrying value net of financing costs. Buybacks (68.9 TTM) more than fund the flat count: shares fell from 178.1M to 175.7M in nine months. Sponsors (Providence Strategic Growth, Silver Lake) hold ~85.7%, so the free float is thin. No forward guidance appears in the 10-K/10-Q text (it is given in 8-K press releases, not in Extracted/); year-1 growth is anchored to reported run-rate (pro forma growth 2.0-3.0% across 2026, revenue growth 2.7% in Q3).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Cash EBITDA margin (adjusted EBITDA less capitalised-commission amortisation less recurring 'non-recurring' costs): 24.7% TTM, rising 2.8pp as transformation costs roughly halve.
base.da_note: TTM continuing D&A 62.9 (10.4%), dominated by acquired-intangible amortisation that is running off; converges on capex.
base.capex_note: PP&E 1.9 plus capitalised software 32.4 TTM = 5.7% of revenue.
base.cash_tax_note: Cash taxes are ~3 a year today (NOLs, amortisation and interest shields). Ramped to a 25% federal-plus-state rate by year 7; the NOL balance was not read from the tax note, so the ramp speed is a judgment.
base.wc_note: Deferred revenue has been flat at ~22 for five years (monthly billing, payments revenue), so there is no prepaid-subscription tailwind; receivables growth has been a small drag.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): net revenue retention has fallen four points in a year, organic growth has halved to ~2-3%, and 2.2x net debt/adjusted EBITDA gears the equity to any further erosion. Base 50%: the current run-rate with modest cost normalisation. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it requires growth re-acceleration and a clean exit from recurring 'one-off' costs at the same time, and neither shows in 2026 results.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
